title: Yosef ben Pakhsas the Priest
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a very pious man during the Tannaim’s period. Jerusalem Talmud Nazir, beginning of chapter 7, Semachot, chapter 4, and Sifra, Emor 9, relate that Yosef ben Pakhsas developed an affliction on his feet. A physician came and amputated the affected limb. He called his son Hunyo: “My son, until now you were obliged to attend me. From now on, leave: a priest may not become impure for a limb severed from his living father.” The sages applied the verse “A righteous man perishes in his righteousness”: the righteous man perishes, but his righteousness (nevertheless) remains with him.

notes.text: The checked Nazir account describes amputation of an afflicted leg, not cutting a thread. It names Yosei ben Pakhsas and the son Nechunya, whereas Hyman has Yosef and Hunyo; these variants remain separate. The supplied plural “feet” is retained in the body.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 7:1 has Yosei ben Pakhsas and Nechunya; Tractate Semachot 4:28 has Yosef Paskas and Nechuni. Both describe cutting the affected leg while leaving a hair-width attachment before the son departs. Hyman’s Yosef ben Pakhsas, Hunyo and plural feet remain as supplied. The exact Sifra Emor 9 locus has not been independently inspected.
